analysis:
Examined both scheduler excerpts against the canonical index and supplied T-041 detail. The change adds single-Mac thought-loop recovery: MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift:1024-1035 resolves an exit policy, disables it for distributed pairs, and shares stop-string scope; :1108-1169 splices a second engine row into the original stream. The continuation preserves cache scope, cache enablement, sampling and donation settings (:1144-1152), waits up to five seconds for first-row release (:1133), and supplies cancellation for both rows (:1123,1161). No concrete regression is established in this scope. Surrounding media paths retain pre-decode admission, memory release, fail-closed model refusal and scoped cache submission; the patch does not change those paths. No authorization, attestation, encryption, root authority or credential-handling changes are visible.
Integration must examine GenerationLoopExitThinkingPolicy, GenerationLoopGuardPolicy, LoopExitThinkingContinuation and bridge admission/retirement together. In particular, the second submission (:1142-1157) omits the first row's usageSignal, tokenConstraint, service reservation, promptWork and distributedRequestOrigin, and sets firstContentDeadline to nil. Verify that splice accounting includes continuation tokens for billing, output budget covers both rows, cancellation/deadline handling remains effective, and fresh admission cannot bypass serving allowances (T-010, A-018, A-009). Verify policy excludes constrained outputs or rebuilds their constraint state; otherwise a continuation could evade JSON/tool enforcement. Also check whether reused stopStringScope correctly reflects the now-closed thought. These are unverified cross-file contracts, not demonstrated missing controls. Cache scope is explicitly retained, so no T-041 isolation regression is shown; continuation cache identity and storage remain outside this excerpt.
